soundness_flags.label: ass:population-selection-margin and ass:intervention-selection-margin
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Chen--Mooij positivity class does not state either a lower bound on population selection prevalence or a uniform lower bound on intervention-specific selection probability; retag these as novel sensitivity restrictions and justify their scientific calibration.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2
soundness_flags.one_line: With Lift(t) defined as existence of a graph-legal fiber point having ratio t, “t is attained iff Lift(t)” and the compactness closure condition are definitional encodings plus routine real-closed-field decidability, not yet a substantive theorem.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 5
soundness_flags.one_line: “C_n and Pi_n shrink to their truths” has no topology or graph-set convergence definition, and universal legal lifting at a fixed (P,q) does not by itself imply endpoint or Hausdorff continuity under simultaneous law and COPAG perturbation.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The proposal does not give a finite, invariant definition of the essential-feature index set e or prove that its Z_e constraints are equivalent to the stated actual-functional-dependence selected-MAG semantics, so the claimed exact stratum is not yet a determinate input language.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Universal graph-legal lifting remains an unresolved premise and is explicitly delegated to Open-ended Question 1.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Compactness, algebraic endpoint attainment, and finite witnesses are claimed only conditional on an affirmative universal legal-lifting resolution.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 25–26, model classes M+(G), Definition 4.3, and Remark 4.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper's positivity conditions are absolute-continuity/strict-density conditions for interventional kernels; it notes positivity of the selected observational law as a consequence, but does not supply a delta lower bound on Pr(S=1) or Pr(S^b=1).
Proposition 2 polynomializes counterfactual statements in a canonical DAG, and Theorem 1 states that Algorithm 2's polynomial program yields sharp lower and upper bounds.
The optimal PAG and neural counterfactual bounds are defined for an observational law faithful to the PAG, and Theorem 3 says the two bounds coincide.

The paper characterizes selected interventional distributions conditional on selection and proves smDG-based indistinguishability under its Observe-and-Do scheme; it does not formulate an absolute selection-probability fiber.
The paper establishes openness and density of faithful distributions in total variation in its unconstrained Bayesian-network setting and discusses the scope of that typicality result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Specify a finite essential-feature index set and prove an iff lemma connecting its Z_e polynomial constraints to the exact selected-MAG induced by structural functions, including off-support functional dependence.

Replace the definitional part of Theorem 2 with a nontrivial certified procedure: an explicit finite formula generator, architecture enumeration bound, and a theorem separating an illegal closure point from every legal lift.

Retag both delta margins as novel sensitivity restrictions, state which empirical or scientific inputs calibrate delta, and separate mere denominator positivity from the stronger uniform-margin restriction.

State Hausdorff or Painleve--Kuratowski convergence for C_n and Pi_n and add the continuity/outer-semicontinuity condition actually needed for endpoint convergence; otherwise retain only finite-sample outer coverage.

recommended_next_step: Revise the exact-stratum semantics, margin tags, and inference convergence claim, then advance the repaired field-level graph-legal-lifting kernel to Stage 0.
